introH2: 🏥 Staying Near BNH Hospital Bangkok — What Are Your Options?
introHtml: BNH Hospital (Bangkok Nursing Home Hospital) at 9/1 Convent Road, Silom, Bang Rak, has served both Thai and international patients for decades. It is a common destination for medical tourism, specialist consultations and annual check-ups — and when you or a family member needs to stay close to the hospital for several days, the choice of nearby accommodation matters a great deal. The Silom–Bang Rak district around the hospital has a healthy range of options: a brand-new boutique hotel that opened in 2021 a 3-minute walk away, a hotel literally on the same street as BNH, a spacious serviced apartment with a full kitchen for multi-week stays, and a 5-star Accor property still within walking distance. This guide rounds up 7 hotels in the Silom–Convent Road area that we have reviewed in depth, every rating drawn from verified guest reviews, every caveat called out honestly. Prices compared across three booking platforms, with direct booking links for all seven.
mrtHtml: BNH Hospital sits on Convent Road, a quieter side street off the main Silom Road in Bang Rak. BTS Sala Daeng station (Silom Line) is roughly 7–10 minutes on foot from BNH, connecting easily to Siam, Asok and Chong Nonsi. MRT Si Lom station is around 5–9 minutes' walk depending on which hotel you choose, and is useful for journeys north–south on the Blue Line. Several hotels in this guide sit on Convent Road or in its immediate side streets, making actual walking times to BNH as short as 2–3 minutes. BTS Chong Nonsi is the nearest sky train station to the Pullman (5 minutes), and is handy if you are arriving from the Sathorn–Narathiwat corridor. From any station in this area you can connect to Suvarnabhumi Airport via BTS to Phaya Thai then the Airport Rail Link, or Grab — typically 30–45 minutes.

entries.storyHtml: PASSA Hotel Bangkok is a 36-room boutique hotel that opened in 2021 at 63 Soi Sala Daeng 2 — just 215 metres from BNH Hospital, a flat 3-minute walk along a quiet side street with no major road crossings. The hotel's calling cards are hand-commissioned floor-by-floor murals (each floor gets its own artist), a rooftop infinity pool with a sunset bar, and an à la carte breakfast served fresh each morning. Guest scores on Booking.com run to 9.4 for service, with reviewers repeatedly singling out staff who remember faces and follow up on requests. A few honest caveats: the rooftop pool is small — it is a place to soak and watch the city, not do laps — a handful of rooms have shown humidity issues (the hotel supplies dehumidifiers on request), and Superior rooms at 23 sqm can feel close during a multi-week stay.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you are staying to support a patient at BNH for several days, book the Deluxe Room (30 sqm) which comes with a bath — the extra space and bathtub make a real difference when you need to decompress after a long day at the hospital. Report any humidity issue to the front desk immediately; staff response is fast.

entries.storyHtml: Le Siam Hotel Silom by PCL has the most straightforward location pitch in this entire guide: it sits at No. 3 Convent Road — the same street as BNH Hospital at No. 9/1 — making it a 250-metre, 3-minute walk along a single shaded footpath, no turns needed. The 55-room, 3-star hotel offers warm teak-toned rooms, Tempur-Pedic mattresses that guests repeatedly praise for comfort, an outdoor pool with a separate children's section, and the Glom Glorm Thai Eatery. Rates start at ฿1,600, considerably below the PASSA next door. What to know before booking: the building is older, and some rooms show wear and the occasional musty note. The pool ladder is steep — less suitable for guests with limited mobility. Breakfast is a paid buffet at ฿390 per person, and reviewers note the selection does not change much day to day.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Check your room on arrival — specifically the AC, any musty smell, and the bathroom seal. Staff resolve issues quickly once flagged. If you are staying for a longer medical trip, consider the One Bedroom Suite (43 sqm) which has a separate sitting area, making it noticeably more liveable than the standard rooms.

entries.storyHtml: Artino Hotel Silom is an 18-room boutique tucked into Soi Phiphat 2, which connects directly to Convent Road — placing BNH Hospital 400 metres away (5-minute walk) while BTS Sala Daeng is just 4 minutes in the other direction. Two things lift it to third place: its 867 Booking.com reviews represent the widest evidence base in this guide, and the rooftop saltwater pool with a close-up view of MahaNakhon Tower is a genuine differentiator that guests rave about. Cook-to-order breakfast and free (limited) parking round out a strong 4-star value case. The honest counter-points: bathrooms are compact and can feel cramped; walls are thin enough to carry corridor noise; and a handful of international reviews mention damage-charge disputes — always photograph the room on arrival.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Free parking is limited — call ahead to confirm a space. The Large Room category gives direct rooftop pool access, well worth the upgrade if an early morning swim is part of your routine. With only 18 rooms, the hotel fills up fast during BNH appointment surges — book early with free cancellation.

entries.storyHtml: Mirth Sathorn Hotel is the physically closest property to BNH Hospital in this guide. Soi Sathorn 4 runs directly behind BNH, putting the front desk just 150 metres — a 2-minute walk — from the hospital entrance, confirmed by multiple reviewers. The 20-room boutique hotel leans into traditional Thai décor: carved teak, four-poster beds, private balconies and a neighbourhood-quiet atmosphere. Rates start at ฿900/night, the lowest in the guide. There is one essential caveat: the shortcut path through Soi Sathorn 4 behind St Andrews school closes around 20:00. After that, returning guests must detour via North Sathorn Road, adding roughly 5–8 minutes. Check this with the front desk before going out in the evening. The score of 7.6 on Agoda — though backed by 1,067 reviews, the most in the guide — indicates recurring trade-offs: thin walls, inconsistent water pressure in some rooms, no pool and no in-room kettle.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Before heading out in the evening, ask the front desk exactly when the Soi Sathorn 4 shortcut closes and which evening route to take back. If you are a light sleeper, request an upper-floor room away from the main corridor — a small hotel, so staff can usually accommodate.

entries.storyHtml: Urbana Sathorn Bangkok is a 4-star serviced apartment complex of 159 suites on South Sathorn Road, approximately 700 metres — an 8-minute walk — from BNH Hospital. The reason it makes this guide is straightforward: every single suite comes with a full-size kitchen including a large refrigerator, a washing machine and dryer, a separate sitting room, and starts at 72 sqm. For a caregiver or patient in town for multi-week treatment, this combination of space and self-sufficiency is difficult to beat anywhere in the area. Facilities include a 25-metre rooftop pool, a fitness centre, a sauna, a squash court, and free parking — rare in Sathorn. Reviewers frequently describe it as 'feeling like having your own apartment.' The caveats are real: the building is ageing, some bathrooms and furniture show use-wear, lifts occasionally play up, and lower-floor rooms pick up South Sathorn Road traffic noise.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Always request a room from the 10th floor up — noticeably quieter and the views dramatically better. The neighbourhood has a wet market and a supermarket within five minutes, so you can take full advantage of the kitchen and keep food costs down during a long stay.

entries.storyHtml: The Inn Saladaeng is a 43-room, 3-star hotel on Sala Daeng Road — an 8-minute walk to BNH Hospital but with the best sky-train access of any hotel in this guide: BTS Sala Daeng 3 minutes, MRT Si Lom 4 minutes. Rates start at ฿1,100/night, making it the second-most affordable option after Mirth. Regular guests note clean rooms, cheerful and helpful staff, and the 24-hour free coffee, tea, biscuits and instant noodles station at the lobby, which turns out to be genuinely useful during long hospital days. The honest picture: rooms are smaller in person than they appear in some platform photos, bathrooms are narrow, and there is no pool, gym or breakfast. Power sockets are limited and the hotel does not supply basic toiletries — bring your own. Walls are thin and some rooms have reported inconsistent hot water.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If bathroom space matters, book the Deluxe Room over the standard Guest Room. Pack a travel multi-plug adapter for the power-socket limitation. Lumphini Park is a 10-minute walk — good for clearing your head after a long day at BNH.

entries.storyHtml: Pullman Bangkok Hotel G is a 469-room, 38-floor Accor property on Silom Road — the only 5-star in this guide — around 800 metres from BNH Hospital, a 10-minute walk via Silom Road turning into Convent Road, perfectly doable without a taxi for most guests. What puts it on this list: Scarlett Wine Bar on the 37th floor is listed in the Michelin Guide Bangkok and offers 360-degree city views that go well beyond the ordinary hotel rooftop; the 25 Degrees restaurant is open 24 hours; EnerGy Fitness runs 24 hours; and G Spa provides a genuine recovery option after a tough day at the hospital. Honest note: the building dates from 1992 and some lower-floor rooms can feel dated with occasional equipment niggles. Reviewers consistently recommend booking floor 26 or above, or upgrading to G Club tier for a noticeably better experience.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Book a room on floor 26 or higher to avoid the dated lower-floor finish that generates most of the negative reviews. Reserve a window table at Scarlett well in advance — especially Friday or Saturday nights when demand is high.

faqTitle: FAQ — Hotels Near BNH Hospital Bangkok: Common Questions

faq.q: Which hotel is the shortest walk from BNH Hospital on Convent Road?
faq.a: Measured by actual distance, Mirth Sathorn Hotel (Soi Sathorn 4, directly behind BNH) is the closest at around 150 metres — a 2-minute walk. However, the shortcut path through Soi Sathorn 4 closes around 20:00, after which guests must take the longer route via North Sathorn Road. For the best balance of proximity, guest score and price, PASSA Hotel Bangkok (215 m, score 8.9) and Le Siam Hotel Silom (250 m, score 8.8, on the same street as BNH) are consistently confirmed by real reviews as the most convenient walkable options.

faq.q: Why is Mirth Sathorn Hotel ranked 4th when it is physically the closest to BNH?
faq.a: Raw distance is one factor but not the only one. Mirth Sathorn's Agoda score is 7.6 — the lowest in this guide across 1,067 reviews — reflecting recurring guest issues including thin walls, inconsistent water pressure and limited amenities. The 20:00 curfew on the Soi Sathorn 4 shortcut also meaningfully affects convenience for evening returns. It is still a solid pick at ฿900 for budget-focused travellers who understand the trade-offs before booking.

faq.q: Which hotel near BNH is best for a long-stay caregiver or recovering patient?
faq.a: For stays of a week or more, Urbana Sathorn Bangkok is the clear recommendation. Every suite comes with a full kitchen, large fridge, washing machine and dryer, and starts at 72 sqm — 8-minute walk from BNH. Facilities include a 25-metre rooftop pool, gym and free parking. For longer medical stays on a tighter budget, Le Siam Hotel Silom's One Bedroom Suite (43 sqm with a sitting room, from ฿2,500) is on the same street as BNH and offers meaningful living space versus the standard room.

faq.q: How easy is it to use the BTS or MRT from hotels near BNH Hospital?
faq.a: Very straightforward. BTS Sala Daeng (Silom Line) connects north to Siam and south to Saphan Taksin and is 3–10 minutes' walk from most hotels in this guide. MRT Si Lom (Blue Line) covers the north–south corridor and is 5–9 minutes from BNH. The Inn Saladaeng (BTS 3 min) and Artino Hotel Silom (BTS 4 min) have the fastest rail connections. For Suvarnabhumi Airport, take BTS to Phaya Thai then the Airport Rail Link — approximately 30–45 minutes total.

faq.q: How do I get from Suvarnabhumi Airport to the BNH area in Silom?
faq.a: The most reliable route is the Airport Rail Link from Suvarnabhumi to Phaya Thai station (approx. 28 minutes, around ฿45–150 depending on service type), then BTS from Phaya Thai to Siam, change to the Silom Line (dark green) and alight at Sala Daeng. Total journey 50–70 minutes, cost roughly ฿100–200. Alternatively, Grab from the airport runs about ฿300–500 and takes 35–60 minutes depending on traffic — direct to your hotel door with no luggage transfers.

faq.q: Is there a 5-star hotel within walking distance of BNH Hospital Bangkok?
faq.a: Yes — Pullman Bangkok Hotel G (188 Silom Road, Accor group) is around 800 metres from BNH, a 10-minute walk along Silom Road into Convent Road. The hotel has 469 rooms, the Michelin Guide-listed Scarlett Wine Bar on floor 37, a 24-hour restaurant and gym, and G Spa. Rates start around ฿2,500/night. Reviewers consistently advise booking rooms on floor 26 or above (or G Club level) to avoid the dated lower-floor fit-out.
